plan: This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and I have no incentive to bid above or below my true value. Bidding my true value ($49) is the dominant strategy—if I bid higher, I risk winning at a price above my value; if I bid lower, I might lose an auction I could have profitably won. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This auction structure mirrors a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own. In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - bidding higher risks overpaying if I win, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my true value and my lower bid. Since my value is $44, I should bid exactly $44 to maximize expected profit.

This auction mechanism functions as a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point is determined by my sealed bid. In second-price auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy since it ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the price I'd pay, and never pay more than my value. Overbidding risks paying more than my value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $22.
